altitude.quote: under construction 4100 meters above sea level at Sierra Negra, Mexico

coordinates.locator: HAWC design/calibration/operation paper, site-description section: "The geographical latitude of the site is 18.99 … The geographical longitude of the HAWC site, 97.31 W."
coordinates.note: Published site coordinate at 0.01° precision (about 1 km), replacing a Nominatim geocode of the Sierra Negra peak 3 km wide; precision_m set to half the rounding step. Previous record: campus point 18.9862137, -97.3151017 at 3000 m precision, sources ['src:cosmic-gamma-hawc-design-paper-arxiv-2013', 'src:cosmic-gamma-nominatim-sierra-negra']; moved 570 m (integrator, 2026-09-21, per docs/atlas-worklog/GEOMETRY_*.md).

summary.plain: The high slope of the Sierra Negra volcano in Mexico where the HAWC observatory's water tanks sit, high enough in the thin air to catch gamma-ray air showers.
summary.technical: HAWC array site on the Sierra Negra volcano, Puebla, Mexico, at 4100 m altitude.
